requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.summary: The analyzer regressed after version 3.1.0: starting with 3.1.1, it stops working when SuppressSourceGeneration is set to true.

hunks.context: This code generation has a minor upfront performance cost.
lines: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
+A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
+No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
+The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
+- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
+- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
+- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

+The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.
+                            continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
+                            continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.

+/// A type that opts out of source generation (https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234).
+/// It must still serialize correctly through the run-time (dynamic) resolver.
+    public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
+        var value = new SuppressedSourceGenerationType { Id = 7, Name = "seven" };
+// Copyright (c) All contributors. All rights reserved.
+// Licensed under the MIT license. See LICENSE file in the project root for full license information.
+/// Verifies that the analyzer keeps validating <c>[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]</c> types
+/// Opting out of source generation only skips generation; the type is still serialized at run time, so its contract must still be checked.
+        // The partial-class requirement (MsgPack011) and the AOT-only checks (MsgPack016, MsgPack017)
+        // only matter when a formatter is generated, so they are not reported for a suppressed type.
+    public string Prop1 { get; init; } = ""some default"";

suspicions.hypothesis: The core regression may remain unfixed for suppressed types whose contracts do not contain duplicate or mixed keys: none of the production hunks changes a SuppressSourceGeneration check or an analyzer entry point, so an existing early return that bypasses collection would still bypass MsgPack003/004/015. The new non-collision analyzer cases should be checked specifically against that early-return path.

README's promise that MsgPack012 still applies to suppressed types may be untrue or untested: the new analyzer suite covers MsgPack003/004/005/015 and the excluded diagnostics, but contains no inaccessible-type case that would require MsgPack012.

The no-source-generation-diagnostics case may still fail because no production hunk conditions MsgPack011, MsgPack016, or MsgPack017 on SuppressSourceGeneration; if those checks currently run for suppressed types, the test and README assert behavior that this diff does not implement.

refusals.question: Does “normal analysis” in REQ-2234.1 mean the reduced diagnostic set documented and tested here, specifically excluding MsgPack011, MsgPack016, and MsgPack017 for suppressed types?
refusals.why: The requirement does not explicitly exempt those diagnostics; choosing which existing diagnostics are dropped is an interpretation of the requirement and an intentional diagnostic-behavior decision for the owner.
refusals.summary: Confirm REQ-2234.1 excludes MsgPack011, MsgPack016, and MsgPack017 for suppressed types

refusals.question: Is it intentional to change invalid-contract recovery for every type processed by TypeCollector, including ordinary generated types, by skipping mixed-key members and discarding later duplicate-key members from the collected model?
refusals.why: These source changes are not limited to SuppressSourceGeneration and can change downstream diagnostics and generation inputs after an error; the generated-type duplicate test also extends the fix beyond the stated analyzer regression. The owner must decide whether that broader behavior change belongs in this fix.
refusals.summary: Decide whether TypeCollector’s broader invalid-contract recovery belongs in this fix

refusals.question: 6 of 10 new tests pass without the change, so the behaviour they test already works at the base. Does the reported problem exist in this base, and what are these tests for?
refusals.why: Tests that pass with the change reverted: SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed, SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType, SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.SuppressedTypeRoundTripsThroughDynamicResolver
refusals.summary: Confirm whether base reproduces regression and explain six already-passing tests
